title: Jess Stacy, Benny Goodman, Paul's wife and the 1934 band's impact
summary: Paul recommended Jess Stacy to Goodman; Paul married Marie Harrison from a Chicago police family; the 1934 band played freely and drew other bandleaders.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well, I mentioned Jess Stacy was on piano. In fact, Paul recommended Jess Stacy to Benny Goodman. And that's where Jess went into Ben Goodman for Paul's recommendation. Of course, Benny Goodman is very good friends with Paul. In fact, Benny played for Paul's wedding when he was in short pants. Really? Yeah, Benny was only at that time 16 years old.
I met Paul's wife. She was the brother of some police captain or something? Yeah, her brother Tom was captain of police
in the first district of Chicago.
That's right. She had two brothers also that were sergeants and was a big police family.
Yeah, I remember. What was their name again?

Harrison's. Tommy Harrison and her name was Marie Harrison. But at that time, Paul had an awful good band and they sort of brought back jazz in that 34 because at that time they were the only band playing what they felt like playing. They weren't told to play this, tell them to play that, just Paul kicked the tunes off and they played what they wanted. And I spoke to a lot of musicians at that time and they all said that this band was probably swinging a jazz band, Dixieland band in the nation at that time because they all used to come watch it. I mean, Earl Heinz, Duke Ellington, all that stood in the kitchen and listened to the band. They all liked it. Bill, do you want to get back to the little label? Southway?
